paragraphs.source_en: If one insists on dissecting their psychology, it comes down to this: they are delighted that Buemon has fallen into trouble. Gentlemen, try asking those ladies, “Do you laugh because you find it amusing when someone else is in distress?” They will call the person who asks such a question a fool; and even if they do not call him a fool, they will say that posing such a question is a deliberate insult to the character of ladies. It may indeed be true that they feel insulted, but it is also true that they laugh at another person’s distress. If that is so, it amounts to saying, “I am now going to show you myself doing something that disgraces my own character, but you are not allowed to say a word about it.” How is their behavior any different from such a declaration? It is the same as making this claim: I shall be a thief, but you must not call me immoral. If you do call me immoral, then you have smeared mud on my face; you have insulted me. Women are always very clever. Their thinking is quite logical: since one has been born human, when one is trampled, kicked, and beaten and no one so much as turns to look, one must be prepared to remain perfectly unconcerned. Not only that, one must also possess the notion that even if spat upon, splashed with filth, and loudly laughed at, one ought to accept it willingly. Without such preparation and such an outlook, it is impossible to associate with those creatures known as clever women. As for Brother Buemon, though he seems terribly abashed because a slight excess on his part has led to a serious affair, he may still think it rude for people to laugh behind his back at his embarrassed state; but that is because he is young and childish. The other side will say that getting angry whenever someone is rude proves he is small-minded, and if he dislikes being called that, he had better behave quietly. Finally, permit me to introduce Buemon’s state of mind. The fellow is worry incarnate. His great head, just as Napoleon’s great head was filled to bursting with ambition, is now almost bursting with worry. The reason his bulbous nose twitches from time to time is that his anxiety has been transmitted to the facial nerves and is acting unconsciously, as though by reflex. He is like a man who has swallowed a large lead bullet, carrying in his belly an intractable hard lump, and for the last two or three days he has been at a loss what to do with it. Driven to the height of anguish, and with no one to devise a good plan for him, he thought that if he went to the teacher called his supervisor, perhaps he might get help. Thus he came to the house of the teacher he ordinarily disliked, bowing his head in supplication. He had completely forgotten how, in his usual days at school, he had teased the supervising teacher and incited his classmates to make trouble for my master. He seems to believe that no matter how much he has teased my master or made trouble for him, since my master bears the title of supervisor, he will surely concern himself with Buemon’s case. He is really quite simple-minded.

paragraphs.source_zh: 如果勉强去解剖她们的心理，那就是对武右卫门君陷入困境而感到得意。诸位，你们可以去问问那些妇女们：“当别人陷入困境时，你们会因为感到有趣而发笑吗？”她们将会把提问的人说成是糊涂虫，即使不说成是糊涂虫吧，也会说提出这样的问题是故意侮辱淑女们的品性。认为侮辱了她们这也许是事实，不过，看到别人陷入困境而发笑，这也是事实。既然是这样，这不就等于说：“现在我自己要做出侮蔑自己品性的事给你们瞧了，但是，就是不准你们说三道四。”她们的行为和这种说法又有什么两样呢？这和下边的主张也是一样的：我做小偷，不过不准你们说我不道德。如果你们说我不道德，那就是向我脸上抹泥，就是侮辱我。女人总是很机灵的。她们的想法也是合乎条理的：既然生而为人，遭受践踏、殴打，而没有人理睬你时，就必须有个满不在乎的心理准备。不但如此，还必须具备这样一种想法：即使被别人吐了一身唾沫，被别人泼了一身臭屎，被人大声嘲笑一番也得甘心承受才行。假如没有这样的心理准备，没有这种想法，那就不可能和那些被称为机灵的女子交往。武右卫门这位老兄，虽然由于做了一点过分的事，搞出了很大问题，因而惶恐万分，但他也许觉得在背后笑话他惶恐的表现是不礼貌的，这是由于他还年轻幼稚的缘故，对方会说他一遇别人不礼貌就生气，说明他气量狭小，如果不愿意别人这样说，那就最好老实一些。最后，请允许我介绍一下武右卫门君的心理活动。这位老兄是处于担心的绝顶。他的那个巨大头脑，正像拿破仑的巨大头脑中被功名心充塞得满满的一样，他的头脑出于担心而几乎要炸裂。他的蒜头鼻子之所以不时扑哧扑哧地掀动着，就是担心的情绪传给了颜面神经，像反射作用一样，它在进行无意识的活动。他就像咽下一个大铅丸，在腹中滞积着一个无可奈何的大硬块，最近两三天，一直不知怎样处理才好。他由于苦闷之极，又没有人替他想出好办法，于是想到假如到班主任老师那里去，也许会得到帮助。这样，他来到自己平素讨厌的老师家里，低头进行恳求。他将他平时在学校里捉弄班主任、唆使其他同学给主人出难题之类的事忘得干干净净。他似乎相信，不管怎样捉弄过主人，怎样给主人出过难题，既然主人的名义是班主任，肯定会替他想办法。真是够单纯的啦。

paragraphs.source_en: Being supervisor is not a post my master took on of his own accord; he accepted it reluctantly under the principal’s orders. It may be compared to the sort of thing Meitei’s uncle’s top hat was: impressive in name only. Of course, a mere name is of no use. If a name were any use in a crisis, Miss Yukie’s marriage interview would long since have succeeded on the strength of her name alone. Buemon not only does exactly as he pleases himself, but also insists that everyone else must help him. He begins from the assumption that people are better than they are. It probably never occurred to him that he might be laughed at. By coming this time to the supervisor’s house, Buemon will surely discover one truth about human beings. Through understanding this truth, he will in the future become a true human being. He will become indifferent to other people’s anxieties, and when others are in trouble he too will laugh loudly and wildly. In this way the world will be filled everywhere with people like the future Buemon, and everywhere with the likes of Mr. Kaneda and his honored wife. For Buemon’s sake, I earnestly hope that he will awaken to this as quickly as possible and become such a true human being. Otherwise, no matter how much he worries, no matter how deeply he repents, and no matter how urgent his desire to abandon evil and turn to good, he will never attain success like Mr. Kaneda’s. No, before long society may even banish him beyond the bounds of human habitation; in that case, expulsion from Bunmei Middle School would be the least of his concerns.

units.source_en: Being supervisor is not a post my master took on of his own accord; he accepted it reluctantly under the principal’s orders.
units.source_zh: 班主任并不是主人主动愿意去当的职务，而是根据校长的命令，不得已承担的。

units.source_en: It may be compared to the sort of thing Meitei’s uncle’s top hat was: impressive in name only.
units.source_zh: 可以说是类似于迷亭的伯父的大礼帽那样的东西，只是名称好听罢了。

units.source_en: Of course, a mere name is of no use.
units.source_zh: 当然只是个名称，是不管用的。

units.source_en: If a name were any use in a crisis, Miss Yukie’s marriage interview would long since have succeeded on the strength of her name alone.
units.source_zh: 如果名称在关键时刻能管用，那么雪江姑娘相亲时只靠她的名字，亲事早就成功啦。

units.source_en: Buemon not only does exactly as he pleases himself, but also insists that everyone else must help him.
units.source_zh: 武右卫门君不但自己想怎么干就怎么干，而且还主张别人都得给他帮忙。

units.source_en: He begins from the assumption that people are better than they are.
units.source_zh: 他是从假定出发把人估计过高。

units.source_en: It probably never occurred to him that he might be laughed at.
units.source_zh: 他大概决没有想到会受别人嘲笑的吧。

units.source_en: By coming this time to the supervisor’s house, Buemon will surely discover one truth about human beings.
units.source_zh: 武右卫门这次来到班主任家，肯定会发现一个关于人的真理。

units.source_en: Through understanding this truth, he will in the future become a true human being.
units.source_zh: 他由于懂得这个真理，将来会成为真正的人。

units.source_en: He will become indifferent to other people’s anxieties, and when others are in trouble he too will laugh loudly and wildly.
units.source_zh: 他会对别人的担心抱以冷漠，别人陷入困境时，他也将会大笑狂笑。

units.source_en: In this way the world will be filled everywhere with people like the future Buemon, and everywhere with the likes of Mr. Kaneda and his honored wife.
units.source_zh: 这样一来，天下到处是武右卫门君这样的人，到处是金田君以及金田的尊夫人一类的人了。

units.source_en: For Buemon’s sake, I earnestly hope that he will awaken to this as quickly as possible and become such a true human being.
units.source_zh: 为了武右卫门君，我真希望他一刻也别犹豫，赶快自觉，做一个这样的真正的人啊。

units.source_en: Otherwise, no matter how much he worries, no matter how deeply he repents, and no matter how urgent his desire to abandon evil and turn to good, he will never attain success like Mr. Kaneda’s.
units.source_zh: 否则的话，即使如何担心，如何后悔，改恶从善之心如何迫切，也决不能取得金田君那样的成功的。

units.source_en: No, before long society may even banish him beyond the bounds of human habitation; in that case, expulsion from Bunmei Middle School would be the least of his concerns.
units.source_zh: 不，甚至社会在不远的将来会把他放逐到人类居住地以外的地方去呢，哪里还顾得上文明中学的退学问题。

paragraphs.source_zh: 班主任并不是主人主动愿意去当的职务，而是根据校长的命令，不得已承担的。可以说是类似于迷亭的伯父的大礼帽那样的东西，只是名称好听罢了。当然只是个名称，是不管用的。如果名称在关键时刻能管用，那么雪江姑娘相亲时只靠她的名字，亲事早就成功啦。武右卫门君不但自己想怎么干就怎么干，而且还主张别人都得给他帮忙。他是从假定出发把人估计过高。他大概决没有想到会受别人嘲笑的吧。武右卫门这次来到班主任家，肯定会发现一个关于人的真理。他由于懂得这个真理，将来会成为真正的人。他会对别人的担心抱以冷漠，别人陷入困境时，他也将会大笑狂笑。这样一来，天下到处是武右卫门君这样的人，到处是金田君以及金田的尊夫人一类的人了。为了武右卫门君，我真希望他一刻也别犹豫，赶快自觉，做一个这样的真正的人啊。否则的话，即使如何担心，如何后悔，改恶从善之心如何迫切，也决不能取得金田君那样的成功的。不，甚至社会在不远的将来会把他放逐到人类居住地以外的地方去呢，哪里还顾得上文明中学的退学问题。

paragraphs.source_en: As I was thinking in this way, I found it most amusing. Just then, the lattice door at the entrance was slid open, and from behind it half a face appeared.
